beats.text: Your closest friends probably live closer than you think.
In nineteen fifty, researchers mapped friendships in a student housing block.
Each box is one apartment. You live here.
Next-door neighbors: forty-one percent became friends.
Two doors away: twenty-two. End of the hall: only ten.
We don't pick friends from everyone. We pick from who we run into. That's why

sources: Festinger, Schachter & Back (1950), Social Pressures in Informal Groups: A Study of Human Factors in Housing – Westgate West (MIT married-student housing): 41 % of next-door neighbors were named as friends, 22 % of those two doors apart, 10 % of those at opposite ends of the hall.
